crop.notes: Full article in five pieces, from headline 'THE PRIZE FIGHT. A Brief but Exciting Mill.' to the closing paragraph.

ocr.notes: Matches the image, but the last paragraph ('The fight was even looked upon in a national sense...' about Allen as an Englishman of the 'Queen's own' and Gallagher as a Fenian) is missing. Small errors: 'Dan Ryan' for Dad Ryan, '6 feet 1 inch' for 6 feet 1½ inches, 'John Lyoney' for John Looney.

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Charlie Gallagher knocked out Tom Allen in the second round on Carroll's Island, below St. Louis, with a right-hand blow behind the ear that left Allen senseless, to the surprise of the fancy.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican—St. Louis, February 24, 1869'. The fight took place the day before, Feb. 23, 1869.

facts.fact: Charlie Gallagher beat Allen in two rounds, about three minutes, knocking him senseless with a right-hander behind the ear
places: Carroll's Island, about one mile below Quarantine, Mississippi River below St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen boarded the steamer Galatea at Bissell's Point, St. Louis, to travel down the river to the fight with Gallagher
Allen and Gallagher were both described as of Cleveland, Ohio; Allen, about 30, claimed to be the English champion of the prize ring
Allen was reported to have said he was England's champion and could whip any Irishman this side of the Atlantic
After Allen revived there was talk of his re-challenging Gallagher for $5,000 a side, but nothing definite was arranged

notes: The 'could whip any Irish &c.' remark is secondhand ('is reported to have said'), so it is not recorded as a quote. Seconds and umpires are left out of the facts.
